name: Vibration
plain: Makes the phone buzz in a pattern.
meaning: Gives tactile feedback only; it cannot read anything. Sites can annoy people or use it for cues, but it also signals the device is a phone.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt; needs a prior tap on the page
access.iframe: Needs user activation in the frame (sticky activation)

firefox.note: Until Firefox 26 included, when the vibration pattern was too long or any of its elements too large, Firefox threw an exception instead of returning <code>false

chrome_android.note: Beginning in Chrome 55, this is not supported in cross-origin iframes. Beginning in Chrome 60, this method requires a user gesture. Otherwise it returns <code>f

samsung.note: Beginning in Chrome 55, this is not supported in cross-origin iframes. Beginning in Chrome 60, this method requires a user gesture. Otherwise it returns <code>f

fields.name: pattern
fields.range: array of up to 10 durations; each up to 10000 ms

limits.headline: Can buzz the phone in a pattern, after you have tapped on the page
limits.user_action: You tap a button or touch the page before it buzzes.
can: Buzz your Android phone in a pattern
Give touch feedback in games, timers and alerts
cannot: Buzz before you have tapped on the page
Buzz on iPhone, because Safari does not offer it
Buzz in current Firefox, which no longer offers it
limits.differs: Android Chrome and Edge allow it. iPhone Safari does not.

story.what_it_is: A site can make your phone buzz in a pattern after a tap.

marketing.name: Vibration API
marketing.pitch: MDN says the API lets a page use the phone's vibration hardware for touch feedback.

story.for_you: A short buzz confirms a tap or warns you about something in the page. Safari on iPhone does not allow it.
story.for_makers: Makers add buzz for touch feedback, alerts and game effects. It works without a prompt but only after you have tapped the page.

use_cases.example: A browser shooter buzzes when you are hit, and a racing game buzzes when you bump a car.
A web workout timer buzzes when it is time to switch moves.
A web app uses short and long buzzes as a code for people who cannot see the screen.
A web ride or food app buzzes when the driver arrives, if the page is open.
A web chat buzzes when a message lands while you are in the app.
A shady page may buzz to trick you into thinking you got a call or alert.

technical_bounds: Needs a prior tap on the page
Android only in practice; ignored on iOS
No effect with ringer off on some devices
